confirmed.title: RLS "to authenticated using(true)" + open signup = any Google/email account on the internet owns all customer data
confirmed.detail: policy "team_access" ... for all to authenticated using (true) with check (true) grants every Supabase identity SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on every row of conversations and messages. Nothing in Postgres ties "authenticated" to "employee" — the only employee check lives in the browser (gateSession, HTML:1004). I probed the project's public settings endpoint (GET /auth/v1/settings with the anon key from HTML:546) and it returns disable_signup:false with google:true and email:true. So the mitigation written in this file's own comment block (schema.sql:103, "disable Allow new users to sign up") was never applied, and identity creation is open to the world. Note this hole does not even depend on that toggle: any ex-employee, or anyone deleted from column O of the sheet, still has a Supabase user row and can keep minting authenticated JWTs forever.
confirmed.attack: 1) Open the public app https://rattana2555.github.io/rattana-app/rattana-unified-inbox.html with any personal Google account and click login (or skip the app entirely and hit https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/auth/v1/authorize?provider=google&redirect_to=<the app URL> directly). 2) Supabase mints the access_token and supabase-js persists it in localStorage under sb-tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg-auth-token BEFORE gateSession ever fetches the sheet; copy it from devtools or the URL fragment. 3) curl -H "apikey: <anon key from HTML:546>" -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" "https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/rest/v1/conversations?select=*" — full customer list; same against /rest/v1/messages?select=* — every message ever exchanged. 4) Because the policy is FOR ALL WITH CHECK(true): DELETE /rest/v1/messages?id=not.is.null wipes the entire inbox, and PATCH/POST let the attacker forge or rewrite staff replies.
confirmed.fix: Stop treating "authenticated" as "staff". Create a server-side allowlist table (staff(email text primary key, active bool)) and rewrite both policies as using (exists (select 1 from public.staff s where s.email = lower(auth.jwt()->>'email') and s.active)) with the same expression in WITH CHECK; split DELETE off into its own restrictive policy or revoke it. Separately set disable_signup=true and restrict the Google provider to the company Workspace domain in Auth settings.
confirmed.whyReal: Could not refute — every load-bearing element was verified. (1) supabase/schema.sql:81-84 does contain `create policy "team_access" ... for all to authenticated using (true) with check (true)` on BOTH conversations and messages; nothing revokes Supabase's default `grant all on tables to authenticated`, so DELETE/UPDATE/INSERT privileges are present. (2) I independently probed the live project: GET https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/auth/v1/settings returns "disable_signup":false, "google":true, "email":true — the compensating control documented in the file's own comment at schema.sql:103 was never applied. (3) No Supabase-side domain restriction exists: GET /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google 302s to accounts.google.com with client_id=418084284284-3hjlnr8ank0fssce81n5m9t7b5eu6bbk, scope=email+profile, and NO `hd` parameter. (4) I confirmed the data plane matches the predicted shape — anon GET /rest/v1/conversations and /rest/v1/messages both return [] with HTTP 200, proving `authenticated` is the sole and only gate; the difference between [] and a full customer dump is possession of any authenticated JWT. (5) The employee check is browser-only: rattana-unified-inbox.html:1004 gateSession() runs only from onAuthStateChange/getSession (lines 1063-1064), i.e. AFTER supabase-js has already persisted the session, and the signOut() calls at lines 1010/1021 neither delete the auth.users row nor prevent re-authentication. The file comment at lines 970-971 ("ด่านจริงคือ RLS") encodes the exact false assumption: RLS here authenticates, it never checks employment. Consequently a resigned employee (column K) or anyone deleted from column O keeps minting valid JWTs forever, and full read + destructive DELETE (`with check(true)` also permits forging staff replies) is reachable via plain curl against PostgREST, bypassing the browser entirely. I deliberately did not create an account to finish the chain end-to-end (account creation is out of bounds for me), but no step required a code path I could not inspect. One honest caveat that narrows blast radius without refuting: I could not determine from outside whether the Google OAuth consent screen is "Internal" (Workspace-only) or "External". If Internal, "any Google account on the internet" narrows to "any @rattanaphaiboon.com Workspace account plus anyone completing email/password signup" — but the ex-employee / removed-from-sheet variant is fully intact either way, and the email provider is enabled with open signup (mailer_autoconfirm:false is incidental friction, not a designed control).

confirmed.title: Employee allowlist is enforced client-side after the JWT is already issued, and the fail-closed signOut does not revoke it
confirmed.detail: gateSession() runs entirely in the browser: the OAuth round-trip has already completed and Supabase has already issued and persisted an authenticated access_token before the CSV fetch at line 1007 happens. The rejection path (line 1010, await sb.auth.signOut()) revokes only the refresh token — Supabase access tokens are stateless HS256 JWTs validated by signature and exp, so the token already sitting in localStorage keeps working against PostgREST, Realtime and Edge Functions until it expires (1h default). Combined with the policy at schema.sql:81, this whole gate is decoration: an attacker never has to run the page's JavaScript at all. The same code is also the only place the resignation column (K) is honoured, so revoking an employee in the sheet revokes nothing server-side.
confirmed.attack: Non-employee signs in with any Google account. Between the redirect landing and the Google Sheets fetch resolving (hundreds of ms, and trivially extended by throttling that one request to Google in devtools) the token is in localStorage. They copy it, close the tab, and use it from curl for the next hour; then they simply log in again for a fresh one. Same for an employee fired yesterday: their Supabase user still exists, so signInWithOAuth still succeeds and the sheet check they never execute never runs.
confirmed.fix: Move the decision server-side. Either sync the sheet into a staff table that RLS consults (see previous finding), or gate the app behind an Edge Function / Auth Hook that refuses to issue a usable session for a non-listed email (custom access token hook that stamps a role claim which RLS requires). The browser-side check should remain only as UX.
confirmed.whyReal:
The claim survives contact with the code, line for line, and I empirically confirmed the one precondition the reviewer left implicit.

Code verified:
- D:\Rattana Pic\rattana-unified-inbox.html:1004-1021 — gateSession() is pure client-side. Line 1007 `const staff = await loadStaff();` is a browser fetch of a public Google Sheet CSV; line 1010 `await sb.auth.signOut();` is the entire rejection path. It runs from onAuthStateChange (line 1063) / getSession() (line 1064), i.e. strictly AFTER Supabase has already exchanged the OAuth result for an authenticated JWT and persisted it under `sb-tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg-auth-token`.
- Line 955 `if((r[COL_QUIT]||'').trim()) return;` (COL_QUIT = 10 = column K) is indeed the only place resignation is honoured, and it only filters a JS Map in the browser. Nothing server-side knows about it.
- D:\Rattana Pic\supabase\schema.sql:81-84 — `create policy "team_access" ... for all to authenticated using (true) with check (true)` on both conversations and messages. Lines 96-97 also `grant execute on ... increment_unread/reset_unread to authenticated`.

The precondition the reviewer assumed, now verified: GET https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/auth/v1/settings returns `"google":true` and `"disable_signup":false`. Signup is open to the entire internet. So the role `authenticated` does not mean "employee" — it means "anyone on Earth with a Google account". The developer's own comments (rattana-unified-inbox.html:969-971 and schema.sql:70-72) assert "ด่านจริงคือ RLS ... to authenticated" — that assumption is exactly what is false, and it is the root cause.

Concrete sequence (no race required — the reviewer's throttling trick is not even the easiest path):
1. Attacker generates a PKCE verifier/challenge and hits https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/auth/v1/authorize?provider=google&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=s256&redirect_to=https://rattana2555.github.io/rattana-app/rattana-unified-inbox.html with any personal Gmail account.
2. Google returns to the allowlisted app URL with `?code=`, visible in the address bar. The attacker reads it and exchanges it via curl at /auth/v1/token?grant_type=pkce. The page's JavaScript — and therefore gateSession() — never executes at all. (Alternative for the lazy: just log in normally and set a devtools breakpoint on line 1010; execution pauses indefinitely before signOut with the token sitting in localStorage.)
3. curl -H "apikey: <the embedded anon key>" -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/rest/v1/messages?select=* → full dump of every customer conversation across LINE/Facebook/TikTok/Shopee. Because the policy is FOR ALL ... WITH CHECK(true), the same token also does UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT on conversations and messages, and can call increment_unread/reset_unread.
4. signOut() at line 1010 revokes only the refresh token; the access token is a stateless HS256 JWT validated by signature+exp, so it keeps working against PostgREST, Realtime and the send-message- Edge Function until expiry (~1h). Repeat step 1 for a fresh one, indefinitely.

Fired-employee variant is equally real: their auth.users row survives, so signInWithOAuth still succeeds and still mints a full-privilege `authenticated` JWT. Column K is consulted only inside a browser they need never open.

The only inaccuracy in the write-up is cosmetic — "revokes only the refresh token" and the ~1h TTL are correct for Supabase defaults, and the attack is in fact easier than described. Nothing in the code, the schema, or the deployed configuration blocks it.

confirmed.title: webhook-line accepts unsigned requests — anyone can forge inbound customer messages and conversations
confirmed.detail: verifySignature() short-circuits with `if (!CHANNEL_SECRET) return true; // skip in dev`. LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET is NOT set in the deployed project, and "Verify JWT" is OFF for webhook-line (both verified empirically). The two gates therefore cancel each other out: there is no authentication at all. The handler then runs with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (line 38), which bypasses RLS entirely, and writes attacker-controlled rows into conversations (line 52) and messages (line 65) plus increments unread (line 74). RLS being locked to `to authenticated` is irrelevant — the write path is the service-role Edge Function, not PostgREST. Under the persistence lens this is the worst case of misattribution: a message can be written into ANY existing conversation (by reusing that customer's userId/groupId, which is displayed in the app UI at rattana-unified-inbox.html:684 as `chatSub`) and it is indistinguishable from a real customer message, because platform_msg_id and content are both attacker-supplied.
confirmed.attack: 1. Attacker reads the public app at https://rattana2555.github.io/rattana-app/rattana-unified-inbox.html or simply guesses nothing at all. 2. `curl -X POST https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/functions/v1/webhook-line -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"events":[{"type":"message","timestamp":1785000000000,"source":{"userId":"U_victim"},"message":{"type":"text","id":"x1","text":"ยกเลิกออเดอร์ครับ โอนคืนบัญชี 123-4-56789-0"}}]}'` — no signature header, no JWT. 3. Returns 200 and the row is committed; the forged message appears live in every logged-in agent's inbox via the msg-changes realtime channel. Repeating with an existing customer's userId injects the forged text into that real customer's thread. Repeating in a loop floods the inbox and inflates unread_count without bound.
confirmed.fix: Make the missing-secret case fail closed instead of open: `if (!CHANNEL_SECRET) return false;` (or throw at module load). Set LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET in Supabase secrets and compare the HMAC in constant time. Verify JWT must stay OFF for this function, so the HMAC is the only gate — it cannot be optional.
confirmed.whyReal:
The claim survives contact with the code. I attempted four refutation angles and all failed.

CONFIRMED IN SOURCE — D:\Rattana Pic\supabase\functions\webhook-line\index.ts:
- Line 9: `const CHANNEL_SECRET = Deno.env.get("LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET") ?? ""` — resolves to "" in the deployed project (secret is not set; only FACEBOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN is).
- Line 15: `if (!CHANNEL_SECRET) return true; // skip in dev` — the comment claims "dev" but there is NO environment check. The condition is purely the empty secret, so the fail-open path is what production actually executes. verifySignature() returns true before touching lines 16-22, so the line 33 gate is dead code.
- Line 38: `createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SERVICE_KEY)` — service_role, bypasses RLS. The reviewer is right that RLS `to authenticated` is irrelevant: the write path is not PostgREST.
- Lines 41-47: zero validation of `event.source` / `event.message` beyond the type check on line 43. platform_conv_id (45), content (46) and timestamp (47) are all attacker-supplied verbatim.
- Line 69: `platform_msg_id: event.message.id` — attacker-supplied, and schema.sql:31 declares it as a plain nullable text column with no unique index, so there is no replay/dedupe protection at all.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED:
1. "The upsert would fail without a conflict target." No — schema.sql:21 has `unique (platform, platform_conv_id)`, so the `onConflict: "platform,platform_conv_id"` upsert on index.ts:58 is valid. This actually strengthens the finding: posting an EXISTING customer's userId does not create a duplicate row, it UPDATES that real customer's conversation (last_message, last_message_at) and returns its real id, into which the forged message is then inserted at line 65-71.
2. "increment_unread is protected." schema.sql:91 revokes it from anon, but schema.sql:93 grants it to service_role — the edge function calls it successfully at index.ts:74. The revoke only blocks direct anon PostgREST RPC, which is not the attack path.
3. "It would not reach agents live." schema.sql:63-66 adds `messages` to the supabase_realtime publication, and rattana-unified-inbox.html:901-902 subscribes `sb.channel('msg-changes')` to INSERT on public.messages. The forged row pushes to every logged-in agent immediately.
4. "The deployed function may differ from the repo file." The task's own verified deployment facts state an unauthenticated POST to webhook-line returned 200 and successfully created a conversation + message + incremented unread. The attack has already been executed once empirically.

CONCRETE SEQUENCE (zero knowledge required): POST https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/functions/v1/webhook-line with `{"events":[{"type":"message","timestamp":<ms>,"source":{"userId":"<id>"},"message":{"type":"text","id":"<any>","text":"<any>"}}]}`, no x-line-signature header and no Authorization header (Verify JWT is OFF). Line 15 returns true, line 33 passes, lines 50-74 commit conversation + message + unread increment under service_role. Looping this floods the inbox and inflates unread_count without bound (schema.sql:47 is an unbounded `unread_count + 1`), and there is no rate limit or source-IP allowlist anywhere in the function.

ONE NUANCE, NOT A REFUTATION: the worst sub-variant — injecting a forged message into a SPECIFIC existing customer's thread — requires knowing that customer's LINE userId (a 33-char opaque id, not guessable). The reviewer's pointer is accurate: rattana-unified-inbox.html:684 renders `p.name + ' · ' + c.uid`, so the id is visible to any agent, in any screenshot, and to anyone who ever operated a LINE integration for that user. That narrows the targeted variant to someone who has seen the UI. The untargeted variants — fabricating arbitrary new "customer" conversations that are indistinguishable from real ones, and flooding/unread inflation — need no prior knowledge whatsoever and are fully anonymous. Severity stays critical: unauthenticated attacker-controlled writes into the production DB with RLS bypassed, on a customer-service system where staff act on message content (the sample payload is a fake refund/bank-account instruction).

confirmed.title: Staff-register gate is client-side only; RLS `to authenticated using(true)` hands every customer conversation to anyone with a Google account
confirmed.detail: schema.sql:81-84 creates `team_access ... for all to authenticated using(true) with check(true)`. The schema comment at lines 70-72 and the HTML comment at rattana-unified-inbox.html:970-971 both assert that this RLS policy is the real gate ("ด่านจริงคือ RLS ฝั่ง Supabase"). That is false. `authenticated` is not "Rattanaphaiboon staff" — it is any identity the Supabase Google provider will mint a JWT for, which by default is every Google account on Earth. The only thing that actually restricts access to staff is gateSession() at rattana-unified-inbox.html:1004-1025, which runs in JavaScript, in the attacker's own browser, AFTER Supabase has already issued the JWT and supabase-js has written it to localStorage. The `sb.auth.signOut()` at line 1010 revokes nothing that the attacker has not already captured. The blast radius is the entire dataset: `messages.content` (every word customers have typed and every word staff replied), `conversations.customer_name`, and `conversations.platform_conv_id` / `customer_id` — the raw LINE userId and Facebook PSID of each customer, which are permanent cross-service identifiers. Because the policy is FOR ALL with `with check(true)`, the same JWT also grants INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on both tables, and schema.sql:93-94 additionally grants `increment_unread` / `reset_unread` to `authenticated`.
confirmed.attack: 1. Open the public page https://rattana2555.github.io/rattana-app/rattana-unified-inbox.html and view source. Copy SUPABASE_URL (line 543) and SUPABASE_ANON (line 546). 2. Do not use the app at all. Hit the auth endpoint directly: https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/auth/v1/authorize?provider=google&redirect_to=http://localhost:8000/ and sign in with any personal gmail account. 3. Read the `access_token` out of the URL fragment on the redirect back. 4. curl -H "apikey: <anon>" -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" "https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/rest/v1/messages?select=*" and the same for `conversations?select=*`. RLS evaluates `using(true)` for role `authenticated` and returns every row. No employee email, no sheet entry, no page interaction required. The same token also works for `PATCH`/`DELETE` and for subscribing to the realtime `messages` stream to watch new customer chats arrive live.
confirmed.fix: Stop treating `authenticated` as an authorization decision. (a) Create a `public.staff(email text primary key)` table populated from the HR sheet by a scheduled server-side job, and rewrite both policies as `using (lower(auth.jwt()->>'email') in (select email from public.staff))` — same for `with check`. (b) In the Supabase dashboard, restrict the Google provider to the company's Workspace domain (or set an allowed-email-domain list) so a personal gmail cannot obtain a JWT at all. (c) Revoke `reset_unread`/`increment_unread` from `authenticated` and expose them only through an Edge Function that re-checks staff membership. The client-side sheet check can stay, but only as UX — never as the boundary.
confirmed.whyReal: Confirmed, not refuted. (1) schema.sql:81-84 is verbatim as claimed: `create policy "team_access" ... for all to authenticated using (true) with check (true)` on both conversations and messages. (2) I queried the live project's public auth settings endpoint (GET /auth/v1/settings) and it returns "disable_signup": false with "google": true AND "email": true — signups are OPEN. The schema's own remediation note at schema.sql:103-104 instructs the operator to disable new signups; that was never applied. So the role `authenticated` genuinely means "any identity Supabase will mint a JWT for", not "Rattanaphaiboon staff". (3) I attempted to refute via a Google hosted-domain restriction: the 302 from /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google contains client_id=418084284284-...&scope=email profile&response_type=code with NO `hd=` parameter, so Supabase imposes no domain filter. Even if the Google Cloud consent screen were "Internal", the email provider is independently open, giving a Google-free path to an authenticated JWT. (4) I confirmed the anon baseline: anon reads on both conversations and messages return [] / HTTP 200, proving there is no second policy layer — flipping the role from anon to authenticated is the entire difference between zero rows and every row. (5) The only staff check, gateSession() at rattana-unified-inbox.html:1004-1025, executes in the attacker's own browser AFTER the JWT is issued; the sb.auth.signOut() at line 1010 revokes only the refresh token, while the access token is a stateless signed JWT that PostgREST validates by signature+exp alone, so it remains usable for its full TTL. The comments at schema.sql:70-72 and rattana-unified-inbox.html:970-971 assert RLS is the real gate, which the code contradicts. Minor imprecision in the reviewer's writeup that does not save it: step 3 says read access_token from the URL fragment, but the flow is response_type=code — the attacker still obtains the token by exchanging the code at /auth/v1/token?grant_type=pkce or by reading the sb-tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg-auth-token entry out of localStorage on the real page. I did NOT actually mint a JWT, because that requires creating an account in the user's production auth system (prohibited, and it would leave a real user row behind); that final step is inferred from a verbatim-read policy plus a verified-open signup setting plus the RLS state given as trusted deployed fact. Blast radius: messages.content (all customer/staff message text), conversations.customer_name, and conversations.platform_conv_id/customer_id (raw LINE userIds and Facebook PSIDs — permanent cross-service identifiers); `for all` + `with check(true)` also grants INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; schema.sql:93-94 grants increment_unread/reset_unread to authenticated; and realtime is enabled on both tables (schema.sql:57-67), so the same token can stream new customer chats live. Fix: replace using(true) with a predicate binding auth.jwt()->>'email' to a server-side staff allowlist table, and/or set disable_signup=true plus restrict the Google provider to the rattanaphaiboon.com domain.

confirmed.title: send-message- performs no authorization at all; "Verify JWT" is satisfied by the anon key published in the HTML
confirmed.detail: The handler reads conversationId/content and immediately acts with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (line 85) — there is no check of who called it, no verification that the caller is a staff member, and no ownership check on the conversation. "Verify JWT ON" is not an authentication control here because the anon key is a valid project-signed JWT embedded in the public page at HTML:546. I confirmed this live: POST to /functions/v1/send-message- with only the anon key as Bearer reaches the handler and executes the service-role SELECT (returned {"error":"not found"} for a bogus UUID, vs 401 UNAUTHORIZED_NO_AUTH_HEADER with no header at all). CORS is Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* (line 76) so it is callable from any origin in a browser too. The frontend itself proves no user binding is expected — HTML:805 falls back to `Bearer ${session?.access_token ?? SUPABASE_ANON}`, i.e. it happily calls this function with the anon key when there is no session. Today the platform tokens are unset so the outbound push fails, but that is a config accident, not a control: the moment LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN / FACEBOOK_PAGE_TOKEN are configured this becomes unauthenticated write access to the company's official LINE OA and Facebook Page.
confirmed.attack: Attacker takes the anon key out of the page source, obtains any conversation id (via the previous finding, or from Realtime), then: curl -X POST https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/functions/v1/send-message- -H "Authorization: Bearer <anon key>" -H "apikey: <anon key>" -d '{"conversationId":"<real uuid>","content":"โอนเงินมาที่บัญชีนี้..."}'. The message is pushed to the customer from the verified company LINE OA / Page — perfect brand-impersonation phishing, and it never appears in the staff inbox because this function no longer writes to the DB (line 113).
confirmed.fix: Validate the caller inside the function: reject when the Authorization bearer is the anon key or has role != 'authenticated', decode the JWT (or call auth.getUser with the caller's token), and confirm the email is in the server-side staff allowlist before touching the service-role client. Keep Verify JWT on, but do not treat it as authorization.
confirmed.whyReal: The claim survives. send-message/index.ts:80 parses conversationId/content straight out of the body and line 85 immediately builds a SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY client — there is no Authorization header read, no auth.getUser(), no staff-membership check, and no binding between caller and conversation anywhere in the file. "Verify JWT ON" authenticates the project, not the caller: the anon key at HTML:546 is a project-signed JWT, and the frontend itself proves no user binding is expected because HTML:805 falls back to `Bearer ${session?.access_token ?? SUPABASE_ANON}`. CORS at line 76 is `*` with `authorization` allowed, so it is browser-callable cross-origin. The comment at lines 113-115 confirms the function no longer writes to `messages`, so a push driven this way never appears in the staff inbox — matching the stated deployed reality. Every file/line anchor in the finding is accurate and I found no compensating control or misreading. Two corrections that reduce reach but do not refute: (1) the fully-anonymous chain does not complete, because per verified deployed reality anon reads return [] and anon RPC 401, the Realtime subscriptions at HTML:875/901 are RLS-filtered by the `TO authenticated` team_access policy, and webhook-line/index.ts:77 returns a bare "OK" without ever leaking the upserted conv.id — so the conversation UUID must come from elsewhere; (2) it is trivially obtained by any authenticated attacker, since the employee-register gate is client-side only while RLS is `USING(true) TO authenticated`, so any Google account holder can read every conversation id and then drive this function. Impact is currently latent only because LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN/FACEBOOK_PAGE_TOKEN are unset, making every sendX throw into the catch at line 108 (sent=false); nothing in the code prevents the send once those secrets are populated, which is the app's evident intent.

confirmed.title: Full HR register of 261 staff (names, nicknames, phones, birthdates, emails) is downloadable by anyone — the sheet URL is in the public HTML and the sheet must stay world-readable for the app to function
confirmed.detail: Line 922 hard-codes `STAFF_SHEET = 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1M6HdISsLN684qRWyQ73CA4AmUzmYtZaOlffDJXZZIXQ/export?format=csv&gid=1364907058'` into a page served from a public GitHub Pages origin. loadStaff() at line 948 fetches it with a plain browser `fetch()`, cross-origin to docs.google.com. That request can only succeed while the sheet is shared "anyone with the link" — so the architecture structurally requires the HR register to remain world-readable. The `export?format=csv` endpoint returns the ENTIRE sheet, not a projection: the code reads only columns E, F, K and O (constants at lines 923-926), but every other column — phone numbers, birthdates, national ID, salary, whatever else the HR sheet carries for all 261 people — is transferred in full into the browser of anyone who loads the page. There is a second leak on the same code path: line 1007 calls `loadStaff()` BEFORE line 1009 decides the user is not staff, so every rejected outsider who completes Google login walks away with the complete register in memory.
confirmed.attack: No account, no session, no Supabase, no JavaScript needed: `curl -L 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1M6HdISsLN684qRWyQ73CA4AmUzmYtZaOlffDJXZZIXQ/export?format=csv&gid=1364907058' -o staff.csv`. The URL is discoverable by anyone who does View Source on the public app, and — because the page is on GitHub Pages — it is also in the crawled/archived HTML (search-engine caches, the public rattana2555/rattana-app repo, the Wayback Machine), so revoking the link later does not undo prior copies. The resulting file is a ready-made phishing and social-engineering target list: real names + nicknames + corporate emails + personal phone numbers, plus column K telling the attacker exactly which staff have already resigned (accounts that may still be live but unmonitored).
confirmed.fix: Remove STAFF_SHEET from the client entirely and set the Google Sheet back to restricted. Replace loadStaff() with a call to a new Edge Function (JWT-verified) that reads the sheet with a Google service account server-side and returns only `{nick, name}` for the caller's own JWT email — never the roster. Better still, sync the sheet into a `public.staff` table on a schedule (server-side) and have the function read that. Then rotate: the register has been publicly reachable, so treat the 261 phone numbers/emails as already disclosed and notify per PDPA obligations.
confirmed.whyReal: Could not refute — confirmed empirically. (1) rattana-unified-inbox.html:922 hard-codes the sheet export URL; loadStaff() at :948 fetches it cross-origin with plain fetch(), so the sheet must stay world-readable for the app to work. (2) An unauthenticated curl with no cookies/session returned HTTP 200, text/csv, 105913 bytes, 261 lines. (3) The deployed public page at https://rattana2555.github.io/rattana-app/rattana-unified-inbox.html returns 200 and contains the sheet ID in its source, so the URL is discoverable via View Source and is also in the public rattana2555/rattana-app repo history and any crawl/archive — prior copies cannot be revoked. (4) Header row (I read only column names + row count, not individual records, and deleted the download afterward): บริษัท, W, รหัสพนักงาน, คำนำหน้าชื่อ, ชื่อ-สกุล, ชื่อเล่น, เบอร์โทร, รหัสค่างาน, เริ่มงาน, ชื่อหัวหน้างาน, ออกจากงาน, BU, สัญชาติ, วันเดือนปีเกิด (พ.ศ.), E-mail, ตำแหน่ง, แผนก, คลังและรหัสแผนกและตำแหน่ง, เพศ. The code reads only indices 4/5/10/14 but the export endpoint ships all 19 columns for ~260 employees: employee ID, full name, nickname, personal phone, date of birth, nationality, gender, corporate email, position, department, supervisor, start date, resignation date. Reviewer overstated on specifics: there is NO national ID and NO salary column (รหัสค่างาน is a job/wage code, not an amount), and it is ~260 staff rows plus a header, not 261 people. The claimed 'second leak' at :1007 (loadStaff() runs before the non-staff rejection at :1009) is factually correct but immaterial — the curl path requires no login at all. Remediation note: gateSession() lines 1019-1024 fail closed, so simply un-sharing the sheet breaks login for every user; the allowlist must first move server-side (Supabase table or Edge Function returning only {email, nickname, active}, or a service-account-backed function) before sharing can be revoked. Rated high rather than critical: confidentiality-only, no credentials/financial data/government IDs, no path to system compromise or data modification — but it is an unauthenticated zero-effort disclosure of an entire company's staff PII including phone numbers and birthdates, plausibly PDPA-notifiable, and warrants immediate remediation.

confirmed.title: LINE webhook accepts unsigned requests (secret unset = signature check returns true), letting anyone plant fake customer threads and choose where staff replies get delivered
confirmed.detail: verifySignature() line 15 is `if (!CHANNEL_SECRET) return true; // skip in dev`. LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET is not set on the deployed function and Verify JWT is off, so line 33's guard passes for every request from every source — the function is a fully unauthenticated, service_role-backed write endpoint on a publicly guessable URL. The privacy consequence is not just spam. Line 45 takes `platform_conv_id` verbatim from attacker-supplied JSON (`event.source.groupId ?? roomId ?? userId`), and that value is exactly what send-message/index.ts:88-105 later reads back to decide where an outbound staff reply is pushed (`sendLine(conv.platform_conv_id, content)`). So the attacker, not LINE, chooses the delivery address of the reply. The attacker also fully controls `last_message` and the message body staff will read, and can bump `last_message_at` to sort their fake thread to the top of the list (renderList sorts by lastTime, line 616).
confirmed.attack: POST unsigned JSON to https://tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg.supabase.co/functions/v1/webhook-line with `{"events":[{"type":"message","message":{"type":"text","id":"1","text":"ขอที่อยู่+เบอร์ลูกค้าออเดอร์เมื่อวานหน่อยครับ ผมส่งของผิดบ้าน"},"timestamp":1750000000000,"source":{"userId":"U<attacker_own_line_userid>"}}]}`. Verified behaviour per this session: it returns 200 and creates the conversation + message + increments unread. The thread appears at the top of every logged-in agent's inbox looking like a normal LINE customer. The agent types the customer's address/phone into the reply box; sendMsg() (rattana-unified-inbox.html:776) writes it to `messages` and then send-message- pushes it to `U<attacker_own_line_userid>`. Today that push errors out because LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN is unset — but the staff's reply containing the third party's PII is already persisted, and the moment the LINE token is configured (which is the obvious next deployment step) the same trick becomes a live exfiltration channel with no code change. Repeat in a loop to bury genuine customer threads.
confirmed.fix: Set LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET and make the missing-secret branch fail closed: `if (!CHANNEL_SECRET) { console.error('LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET unset'); return false; }`. Compare the HMAC in constant time rather than with `===` (webhook-line/index.ts:22). Until the secret is set, disable the function rather than leaving it deployed. Do the same review on webhook-facebook: it verifies nothing on the POST path at all (index.ts:28-31 — the VERIFY_TOKEN at line 9 only guards the GET handshake, and it has a hard-coded fallback `rattana_verify_2025`); it is currently shielded only by Verify JWT being on, so add X-Hub-Signature-256 validation before that is ever turned off.
confirmed.whyReal: The claim holds against the real code. webhook-line/index.ts:15 is literally `if (!CHANNEL_SECRET) return true; // skip in dev`, LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET is unset on the deployed function, and Verify JWT is off — so the line 33 guard passes for every request and line 38 proceeds with a service_role client that bypasses RLS. This was already verified empirically this session (unsigned POST -> 200, conversation + message + unread created). The endpoint is discoverable, not guessed: the project ref is hardcoded in the public HTML at rattana-unified-inbox.html:543 and the function name webhook-line is written into the committed schema.sql:105. Every downstream link checks out: index.ts:45 takes platform_conv_id verbatim from attacker JSON and schema.sql:21 has unique(platform, platform_conv_id) so the upsert succeeds with an attacker-owned key; index.ts:56-57 writes attacker-controlled last_message and last_message_at, and the frontend orders by last_message_at desc (line 580) then re-sorts by lastTime (line 616), pinning the fake thread to the top of every agent's inbox; send-message/index.ts:88-101 reads that same platform_conv_id back and passes it directly to sendLine(to, text), so the attacker supplies the reply destination. One correction to the reviewer's framing: the exfiltration is latent, not live. LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN is unset, so sendLine sends an empty Bearer and LINE rejects it (throw at send-message/index.ts:26), and the attacker cannot read the staff reply back out either (RLS is `to authenticated`; anon reads return [] as verified). The redirect activates the moment that token is configured, with no code change. What is exploitable today on its own is still real: an unauthenticated, service_role-backed write endpoint on a public URL that lets anyone inject arbitrary threads and message bodies that render as genuine LINE customers, bump them to the top of the list, inflate unread counts, and use the staff inbox as a trusted phishing/social-engineering delivery channel, with no rate limiting and no dedupe on platform_msg_id. Fix: fail closed (`if (!CHANNEL_SECRET) return false;`) and set the secret.

refuted.title: send-message- can be invoked by anyone holding the public anon key, and leaves no DB record of what was sent
refuted.why: The attack's terminal step cannot be carried out. Every outbound path in send-message/index.ts requires a platform token, and per the verified deployment facts the ONLY secret set is FACEBOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN — so LINE_TOKEN, FB_TOKEN, TT_TOKEN, SHOPEE_TOKEN and TTS_TOKEN (lines 13-17) are all the empty string. Tracing the switch at lines 100-107: sendLine posts 'Authorization: Bearer ' (empty) to the LINE push API -> 401 -> !res.ok -> throw at line 26; sendFacebook posts '?access_token=' (empty) -> 400 -> throw at line 39; tiktok/shopee/tiktokshop fail identically and have no webhook ingest deployed so no such conversations can exist. Every throw is caught at line 108, sent stays false, and the function returns {sent:false, error:"LINE error: ..."}. No text reaches any customer — for the attacker OR for a legitimate employee. The claimed critical impact (unauthorized message delivered to a real customer with zero audit trail) therefore cannot occur; there is no delivery to audit. What an anon-key holder actually obtains is a 404-vs-200 existence oracle on a UUID they must already possess, with a response body containing only the platform's own rejection text — no platform_conv_id, no customer identity, no secret is echoed. Two further corrections: (1) the "no DB record" property is not a defect in the legitimate path — the frontend inserts the messages row with status 'sending' at rattana-unified-inbox.html:776-782 and updates conversations.last_message at 792-794 BEFORE invoking the function, which is exactly what the comment at index.ts:113-115 documents and which prevents a duplicate-bubble bug; the reviewer inverts the intent of a correct change. (2) The finding asserts "Verify JWT (ON for this function)" as fact, but the confirmed deployment facts state JWT status only for webhook-line (OFF) and webhook-facebook (ON) — nothing about send-message-; that premise is assumed, though it does not change the outcome since the anon key would pass either way. Residual truth worth keeping at low severity: the handler genuinely performs no caller authorization (line 80 destructures the body and never inspects JWT claims, employee registration, or conversation ownership). That gap is inert today and becomes exploitable only once LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN is configured, so it should be fixed in the same change that enables LINE sending. As filed — critical, presently exploitable, message reaching the customer — the finding does not survive contact with the deployment.

refuted.title: Realtime INSERT echo duplicates the sender's own message; the sent_at dedup fallback can never match
refuted.why:
The finding depends on a race that the deployed pipeline makes structurally unwinnable, and its only real observation (the dead sent_at branch) is a redundant fallback with no consequence.

1) Dedup branch 1 covers every ordering that can actually occur. D:\Rattana Pic\rattana-unified-inbox.html:776-790 — the insert is awaited and `local.id = saved.id` is assigned the moment the PostgREST response resolves. From that instant on, the realtime echo matches `x.id===m.id` at line 907 and is dropped. The vulnerable window is exactly "insert HTTP response still in flight."

2) The Realtime echo cannot beat that response. Both the PostgREST response and the Realtime event originate from the same commit in the same Supabase project (tsudgtzcskoopbymklfg) and share the identical downstream network leg to the browser. The PostgREST response is emitted at commit and travels one way. The Realtime event must additionally be decoded out of the WAL by the Realtime service (replication-slot poll tick, ~100ms class), be RLS-re-evaluated per subscriber — RLS is enabled here, policy "team_access" FOR ALL TO authenticated (supabase\schema.sql:83-84), so the row is re-checked before broadcast — then encoded and fanned out, and only then traverses the same wire. Realtime delivery = PostgREST delivery + polling + RLS + fanout. The reviewer's premise ("websocket delivers the echo ~50ms later, before the insert response returns") inverts the causality: the echo does not exist until after the commit that also releases the HTTP response. The claim "on a busy connection this happens on most sends" is backwards — a busy/lossy connection delays the websocket frame at least as much as the HTTP response, since both cross the same link.

3) The sent_at claim is technically correct but inert. `new Date().toISOString()` (line 763) ends in Z while Realtime renders timestamptz as '... +00', so that branch never matches. But it is a belt-and-braces fallback behind the id check; its failure produces no observable behaviour because branch 1 already handles the realistic case. Same for rows from loadMsgs (line 604) — those carry ids, so they dedup by id.

4) Even in a pathological stall (TCP retransmit delaying the insert response by hundreds of ms), the blast radius is a render artifact, not a messaging defect: only one call to FN_SEND is made (line 800), so the customer can never receive the text twice, and the duplicate is wiped by the next loadMsgs, which reassigns msgCache[convId] wholesale (line 604) on the next open of the conversation. The two copies are also visually distinguishable (one 🕘, one ✓✓), contradicting "the agent cannot tell."

Conclusion: dead fallback code, not a high-severity duplicate-message defect. Worth tidying (compare epoch millis instead of strings) but not a real failure.
